findings.title: Superusers without a membership cause AttributeError on organization_context.member
findings.body: `enable_advanced` evaluates `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. The `or` only short-circuits for superusers, so a non-superuser path reaches `.member.has_global_access`. For an RpcUserOrganizationContext where `member` is None (a user with no membership in the org, who is then allowed by OrganizationAuditPermission only through other means), this raises AttributeError and returns a 500. The check should guard against a None member explicitly.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime sort keys; ?optimized_pagination=true 500s on audit logs
findings.body: The audit log endpoint routes `optimized_pagination=true` to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. Its get_item_key calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the raw attribute, which is a datetime for AuditLogEntry.datetime. That raises TypeError on any page with results. Unlike DateTimePaginator, it never converts datetimes to a numeric timestamp, so the new code path is broken for its only caller.

findings.title: Negative offset from user-supplied cursor is not rejected for prev cursors, causing a 500
findings.body: Cursor.from_string accepts any integer offset, including negatives, and Cursor.__init__ no longer rejects them. In BasePaginator.get_result, when cursor.is_prev is True the code uses `start_offset = offset` unchanged, so a negative value goes straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django raises on negative slice indices, so an attacker or a malformed client cursor produces a server error on every paginated endpoint that uses BasePaginator. The removed `if self.offset < 0` guard on other paginators is no longer applied here either.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch relies on a false claim that permissions are enforced at queryset level
findings.body: The enable_advanced_features branch allows arbitrary negative offsets and justifies it with 'permissions are checked at the queryset level'. Nothing in this paginator checks permissions; it only slices whatever queryset it is given. Any caller that sets enable_advanced_features=True gets unbounded negative-index access with no bounds or permission check in the code, and the comment would mislead future maintainers into relying on it. Also, Django does not support negative indexing in slices, so this branch itself raises.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result wholesale, with divergent behavior
findings.body: The new class copies nearly all of BasePaginator.get_result and get_item_key but has already diverged (negative-offset branch, different count_hits/max_hits handling, no datetime support). Fixes applied to one copy will not reach the other, and the endpoint now has two paginators for the same purpose. The 'optimized' name also implies a performance gain that the code does not provide; it is a copy of the same query path plus a negative-offset feature.

findings.title: zunionstore sums scores of duplicate members, corrupting end-timestamp ordering
findings.body: zunionstore uses the default AGGREGATE SUM. When the same span payload exists in both the destination set and the merged set (for example a redelivered Kafka message, or a span re-added after a redirect), its score becomes the sum of the two timestamps rather than the latest one. The scores are later used by zpopmin for eviction and the code relies on them as end timestamps, so the eviction order becomes wrong. The same issue applies at line 53. An explicit AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) is needed.

findings.title: Spans beyond 1000 are silently evicted with no metric or log
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin removes the lowest-scored (oldest) spans without any metric, log, or counter. Previously the Python side logged 'segment_span_count_exceeded' and dropped the whole segment; that check was deleted in buffer.py. Data loss is now invisible in operations, and the Python `max_segment_spans` parameter (buffer.py line 150) is left as dead config that no longer matches the hardcoded 1000 limit in Lua.

findings.title: Redirect-depth loop limit lowered from 10000 to 1000 and its explanatory comment removed
findings.body: The loop bound was reduced from 10000 to 1000 and the comment about segment trees deeper than the limit was deleted. Trees deeper than 1000 hops will now be joined incorrectly, silently, with no note in the code. This is an unrelated behavior change folded into an eviction PR, and it should either be justified and documented or reverted.

findings.title: New required field end_timestamp_precise on Span breaks construction and consumer on older messages
findings.body: Span gains a required `end_timestamp_precise: float` positional field. Any external caller constructing Span without it now fails with TypeError. In factory.py process_batch, `val['end_timestamp_precise']` is a hard KeyError, so a single span message from Relay that lacks the field will crash the consumer rather than being handled. This is a contract change that is not guarded or documented.

findings.title: max_segment_spans constructor argument is now unused
findings.body: The `max_segment_spans` parameter is still accepted and stored but is no longer read anywhere after the span-count check was removed from _load_segment_data. Callers who configure it will believe a limit is enforced when it is not; the limit is now the hardcoded 1000 in the Lua script.

findings.title: No test covers the new 1000-span eviction or the score-aggregation behavior
findings.body: The PR adds zpopmin eviction at 1000 spans and changes merge semantics to zunionstore, but no test exercises a segment above the cap or a merge where duplicate payloads occur. The existing tests only use 3-5 spans. Neither the eviction order nor the score sum behavior is verified.

findings.title: No tests for negative cursor offsets or the optimized audit-log path
findings.body: The new negative-offset and OptimizedCursorPaginator code paths, and the optimized_pagination query parameter on the audit log endpoint, have no tests. The datetime TypeError and the negative-offset 500 would have been caught by a simple test.
